title: Bounded relative derivative on the unit interval bounds the endpoint increment
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field] with their usual absolute values. Let $g,d:\mathbf R\to\mathbf C$ and $C\geq0$. Suppose that, for every $t\in[0,1]$, $d(t)$ is the derivative of $g$ relative to $[0,1]$, meaning $$\lim_{s\to t,\ s\in[0,1],\ s\ne t}\frac{g(s)-g(t)-(s-t)d(t)}{s-t}=0.$$ Suppose also that $|d(t)|\leq C$ for every $0\leq t<1$. Then $$|g(1)-g(0)|\leq C.$$
